CausalChain: 3D scaffold formation -> Enhanced cell–cell/ECM interactions & robust tight junction formation -> Activation of integrin/FAK signaling -> Subsequent activation of Wnt/β-catenin and YAP/TAZ pathways -> Epigenetic modifications at CYP gene promoters (increased histone acetylation, decreased DNA methylation) -> Increased CYP expression and improved drug metabolism modeling
Hypothesis: We hypothesize that culturing HepG2 cells within a custom-engineered 3D hydrogel scaffold—with precisely adjustable mechanical properties and specific biochemical ligands—will enhance cell–cell and cell–ECM interactions, thereby promoting robust tight junction formation that mimics in vivo hepatocyte architecture. This physical reorganization will first engage integrin-mediated FAK signaling, setting the stage for the activation of mechanotransductive pathways, specifically Wnt/β-catenin and YAP/TAZ cascades. The dual and sequential activation of these pathways is expected to induce targeted epigenetic reprogramming at the promoters of CYP genes, evidenced by increased histone acetylation and reduced DNA methylation. To robustly test this hypothesis, we will employ modular experimental designs using high-resolution, time-lapse high-content imaging, CRISPR-based reporter assays, real-time PCR, and ChIP-seq analyses, along with targeted inhibition of the implicated pathways. The integration of these contemporary technological capabilities will not only provide temporal resolution and mechanistic insights but will also facilitate iterative optimization of the scaffold design, ultimately yielding a highly faithful HepG2 model for human hepatocyte drug metabolism.
Abstract: We propose that a custom‐designed 3D hydrogel scaffold with tunable stiffness, porosity, and biochemical cues can recapitulate key aspects of the liver’s microenvironment and thereby promote physiologically relevant HepG2 behavior. Specifically, our approach aims to enhance cell–cell and cell–ECM interactions to restore robust tight junction formation, followed by sequential activation of mechanotransductive signaling cascades—including integrin/FAK mediated stimulation upstream of the canonical Wnt/β‐catenin and YAP/TAZ pathways. We hypothesize that this orchestrated signaling cascade triggers targeted epigenetic modifications (i.e. increased histone acetylation and decreased DNA methylation) at cytochrome P450 (CYP) gene promoters, ultimately leading to elevated CYP expression and improved drug metabolism modeling. To validate the mechanistic cascade, we will integrate state‐of‐the‐art technologies such as high-content time-lapse imaging, CRISPR-based pathway reporters, real-time PCR, and ChIP-seq, complemented by pathway-specific inhibition studies using genetic and chemical approaches. This modular and temporally resolved strategy not only tests the causal relationships of scaffold-induced physical cues and biochemical signaling but also exploits contemporary microfluidic platforms for iterative scaffold optimization, thereby advancing the fidelity of the HepG2 model in pharmacological applications.
Orignal_vs_New: The original hypothesis proposed that a precisely engineered 3D scaffold would enhance cell–cell interactions and tight junction formation to activate both Wnt/β-catenin and YAP/TAZ pathways, thereby inducing epigenetic changes at CYP promoters. The revised hypothesis retains these key elements but refines the causal chain by: (1) emphasizing the role of finely tuned scaffold mechanical properties and biochemical cues in recapitulating the in vivo microenvironment; (2) introducing integrin/FAK signaling as an upstream mediator that bridges enhanced physical interactions with downstream mechanotransduction; (3) distinctly outlining a sequential activation cascade, enhancing the specificity of the link between physical cues and epigenetic modifications; and (4) incorporating additional contemporary technologies (e.g., CRISPR-based reporters, microfluidic platforms) and modular experimental designs to enable precise, temporally resolved validation. These changes address the review comments by explicitly dissecting the mechanistic steps, introducing intermediate controls, and enhancing the practical implementability of the overall experimental strategy.
